transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: What do you think: does coffee improve exam results?

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: What evidence would help us decide?

transcript.speaker: learner
transcript.text: Can you give me some evidence?

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Studies show correlation but not causation. What else could explain better exam performance?

transcript.speaker: learner
transcript.text: Maybe people who drink coffee also study more.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Good. How would we test whether studying is the real cause?

transcript.speaker: learner
transcript.text: Compare coffee groups but control for study hours.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Is a self-report survey reliable evidence for coffee consumption?

transcript.speaker: learner
transcript.text: No, people might not remember accurately; the source is not reliable.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Here is a counterexample. Would you revise your conclusion?

transcript.speaker: learner
transcript.text: Yes, I'd revise my view; now I think it depends.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: What is still uncertain in your conclusion?

transcript.speaker: learner
transcript.text: I'm uncertain about whether it applies to all subjects.
